html:
Tupaia was a Polynesian navigator and priest from the island of Raʻiātea in the Society Islands who sailed with James Cook on the Endeavour in 1769 and 1770.

He was an arioi, a member of a religious order, and an adviser at the court of Tahiti when the British arrived. He knew the stars, winds and islands of a huge part of the Pacific. When Cook left Tahiti, the naturalist Joseph Banks took him aboard. With Cook he drew a chart of some 74 islands spread across thousands of kilometres, known as Tupaia's map, one of the few records of Polynesian geographic knowledge.

In New Zealand, his language was close enough to that of the Māori that he could talk with them, and he acted as interpreter and go between. Māori remembered him long after; some thought he, not Cook, led the ship. He died of disease at Batavia in December 1770 on the voyage home. His knowledge supports what Polynesian navigation achieved without instruments.
sum: Tupaia was a Polynesian navigator and priest from the island of Raʻiātea in the Society Islands who sailed with James Cook on the Endeavour in 1769 and 1770.
